original_question: For random point sets on the sphere, such as i.i.d. uniform points or points from a determinantal point process, can the quality of the configuration be quantified through the positivity of the associated interpolation integration weights or through how close those weights are to 1/N?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Question 6.1 (Jordi Marzo), in the section titled "Integration weights."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant open problem about random point configurations on the sphere, includes the two random models named in the paper (uniform i.i.d. points and determinantal point processes), and focuses on exactly the two quality indicators singled out there: positivity of the interpolation integration weights and closeness of those weights to 1/N.
missing_details: The paper works on a sphere S^r and fixes an interpolation degree n.
The number of points is not arbitrary: one takes N = dim P_n^r, where P_n^r is the space of spherical polynomials on S^r of degree at most n.
The points must form a fundamental system, meaning the interpolation matrix is nonsingular.
The associated fundamental Lagrange polynomials must be specified: \ell_i \in P_n^r and \ell_i(x_j) = \delta_{ij}.
The relevant weights are specifically the interpolation weights w_i = \int_{S^r} \ell_i(x)\,d\sigma(x).
The measure \sigma on S^r is part of the setup; Section 6 writes d\sigma and compares the weights to 1/N, which makes the intended normalization implicit rather than explicit there.
The paper's question is about random N-point interpolation configurations on the sphere in this exact setup, not about arbitrary random sample sizes.
The paper does not prescribe a particular probabilistic regime such as expectation, high probability, or almost-sure asymptotics, so a faithful stand-alone formulation should keep that openness.
refined_question: Fix r and n, let P_n^r denote the space of spherical polynomials on S^r of degree at most n, and set N = dim P_n^r. If X_N = {x_1,\ldots,x_N} \subset S^r is a random fundamental system of N points on the sphere—for example, N uniform i.i.d. points or N points drawn from a determinantal point process—and if {\ell_i}_{i=1}^N \subset P_n^r is the associated Lagrange basis satisfying \ell_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}, with interpolation weights w_i = \int_{S^r} \ell_i(x)\,d\sigma(x), can one quantify the quality of the random configuration in terms of whether the weights w_i are positive, or in terms of how close they are to the uniform value 1/N?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Section 6 open problem, not the material in Section 1. In Section 6, the paper first defines the interpolation setting: P_n^r, the number of nodes N = dim P_n^r, fundamental systems of points, the associated Lagrange polynomials, and the integration weights w_i. It then gives the motivating context that Fekete points have positive weights and weights close to 1/N in a known case, and finally asks whether analogous notions can quantify the quality of random spherical point sets coming from uniform i.i.d. sampling or determinantal point processes. So your draft is already very close in substance, but it is not fully stand-alone until the interpolation setup and the exact meaning of the weights are made explicit.
